_method_version: 2.0.0 reads the whole FDA feed. 1.0.0 (never pushed) read one page of a two-page feed -- the lexically newest capture file, which is page two: 619 of 1,619 rows, 148 of 206 substances -- and every FDA number in it, the 88%-against-4% cliff included, was computed on that half. On the full register the cliff is 95% against 16%, the concentration finding falls to p = 0.047 and is demoted to artifacts/charts/negative/, and the recipe absorbs a sibling draft (shortage-memory) on what the registers retain and what a shortage lasts. The substance key is the full RxNorm ingredient SET, as in 1.0.0. The revision diff is keyed on the statutory stream, without which 34 packages carrying both a shortage row and a discontinuance row read as revisions.

wss-drug-scarcity.what: national drug-shortage registers -- FDA (openFDA JSON, two pages per run), ANSM (HTML table), TGA (JSON literal inlined in HTML) -- plus FDA inspections, warning letters, recalls, import alert 66-40 and Drugs@FDA marketing-status counts for a 304-molecule cohort
wss-drug-scarcity.role: CAPTURE -- none of the three registers publishes its own history; a resolved shortage leaves the page, which is one of the findings
wss-drug-scarcity.note: not vendored here; fetch.py clones it to artifacts/data/wss-drug-scarcity, or set $WSS_DRUG_SCARCITY
wss-drug-scarcity.inspection_fiscal_years: 2009-2026, complete; each file reports totalrecordcount == resultcount, so no page is truncated

rxnav.what: NLM RxNav: drug name -> RxNorm ingredient codes
rxnav.role: ENRICHMENT -- re-fetchable, no key, NLM keeps its own history
rxnav.key: the full ingredient SET, not the first ingredient

cms_nadac.what: CMS National Average Drug Acquisition Cost, 2026 file dated 09-09-2026
cms_nadac.role: TESTED AND REJECTED -- joins 39% of shortage package NDCs and 18% of the injectable ones, because it prices retail pharmacy and hospital injectables move through GPO contracts it does not observe.

figures.1-what-to-do: one reporting firm predicts a permanent exit at 95% against 16%
figures.2-paediatric: nothing carrying the paediatric flag is being discontinued
figures.3-duration: an Australian shortage lasts about a year; the register's resolved rows say two months
figures.4-memory: no register keeps a resolved shortage for more than about a year
figures.negative/: five worked failures: two pretty tables, two single axes, one half-register result
